speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Finance whether the Ministry will regularly review the Government's commitment to reduce socio-economic inequality and publish the results of such reviews in light of recent findings from a study by Oxfam and Development Finance International that ranks Singapore in 86th placing in the world in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our concern underpins the design of many of our policies and schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our key strategy for tackling inequality is to ensure that all Singaporeans, especially those who are less well off, are able to access good opportunities, earn higher incomes and enjoy a higher standard of living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We do this by providing the necessary support to our citizens at various stages of life, with more support going to the disadvantaged and vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We invest heavily in education so that every child, regardless of socio-economic background, can have access to a good education and develop to his full potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Children from lower-income families receive even more support through the Ministry of Education's Financial Assistance Scheme and bursaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Students with more needs receive additional support through various support programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: These ensure that we preserve social mobility for our next generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: For workers, we introduced the SkillsFuture movement to support skills upgrading so that they can take on better jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We also have the Progressive Wage Model to help lower-wage workers upskill and earn better wages, and Workfare to supplement their income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In the last five years, incomes of lower-wage workers have grown in tandem with median income growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: For those in their silver years, we have introduced the Silver Support Scheme to provide additional support to seniors who have low incomes through life and have little family support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our means-tested health and long-term care subsidies also ensure that those with lower income receive more assistance, while the Goods and Services Tax Voucher scheme supports lower-income families with their day-to-day expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: All these schemes add up to a system that is highly progressive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Mr Perera referred to the ranking by Oxfam and Development Finance International.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The rankings were based on the absolute amount of social spending, with the assumption that the higher the level of spending, the better will be the situation, regardless of whether the spending leads to effective outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The authors have acknowledged the limitations of their study in representing the different circumstances of individual countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This is the case for Singapore, where we target our subsidies and assistance to those who are more needy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This focused approach to reducing inequality enables us to keep our tax burden low while ensuring our social expenditure is prudent, fair and progressive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our approach has served us well so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: We have kept inequality in check, even as income gaps widen elsewhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our Gini coefficient has moderated over the last five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Government has been and remains committed to addressing inequality.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is a field where I think the policy is evolving worldwide; there are different innovations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, how confident is the Government that it is being done?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And to link to that, my second question would be: would the Government consider publishing at regular intervals a report which measures the state of equality of opportunity, looking at indicators – not just the indicators that the Senior Minister of State mentioned like absolute incomes – but also measures like social mobility which are more infrequently measured at the current point.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could the Government consider that kind of regular measurement publication and public debate on this issue, given the importance of the issue and how it cuts across so many other areas of policy?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the reason why every year, during Budget, we review what we can do better.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is part of each Ministry's duty and responsibility to see where the gaps are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in other words, this is not something we do every five years or every 10 years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is part and parcel of the day-to-day work of the Ministries, and we look at it every Budget as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Occasionally, we may have bigger reviews but it is really something that is done each and every day of the Ministries' work.
